author: product-requirements-expert
title: Staff can cancel an upcoming visit from the owner's record
summary: The owner's record offers a cancel action beside each upcoming visit of each pet. Cancelling takes that visit off the pet's record and confirms on the owner's record. A visit dated today or earlier is history: it carries no cancel action, and a direct cancellation request for it is refused.
acceptance_criteria: given a pet with an upcoming visit, when the owner's record is opened, then a cancel action is offered beside that visit
given a pet with a visit dated today or earlier, when the owner's record is opened, then no cancel action is offered beside that visit
given an upcoming visit, when it is cancelled, then the owner's record is shown again, the cancellation is confirmed there, and the visit no longer appears under its pet
given a cancelled visit, when a new visit is booked for the same pet, then the cancelled visit is not among the earlier visits shown
given a visit dated today or earlier, when its cancellation is requested directly, then the request is refused and the visit remains on the record
edge case 3: the date boundary is the one booking enforces — a visit dated today is past, not upcoming
edge case 4: cancelling one visit leaves the pet, the owner, and that pet's other visits untouched
edge case 5: a request to cancel a visit belonging to a different owner's pet than the one named is refused
edge case 6: a repeated request to cancel a visit already cancelled is refused rather than confirmed a second time
non_goals: amending a visit — changing its date, its description, or the pet it stands against (NG-5)
any trace of a cancelled visit: no cancellation log, no reason, no undo, no view of what was cancelled (NG-10)
cancelling a visit from the booking page; the action lives on the owner's record only
deleting an owner or a pet (NG-4)
cancelling or otherwise altering a visit dated today or earlier
notes: NG-4 and NG-5 declined this capability; both were derived from observed absence, not from a decision, and the request settles them. NG-4 now covers owners and pets only, NG-5 covers amendment only, and NG-10 records the declined cancellation trace. Rationale: docs/adr/2026-08-05-non-goal-visit-amendment.md. REQ-LANG-002 binds this slice: the cancel label and the confirmation are user-facing wording, so no text may be hard-coded into the page and every supported language needs the new keys. docs/adr/README.md still needs an index row for the new ADR — outside this agent's write scope.

author: system-design-expert
architectural_fit: Cancellation is the codebase's first removal flow, so the slice lands on new ground in two places and reuses existing shape everywhere else. New ground: the Owner aggregate gains a cancellation, and the pet-to-visit mapping gains orphan removal. Recorded in docs/adr/2026-08-05-visit-cancellation-through-the-owner-aggregate.md, with system-design.md updated at Contracts (invariants paragraph plus a VisitCancellationController row) and Persistence. Reused shape: OwnerRepository stays the only write path into the owner-pet-visit graph, a cancellation is an ordinary owner save, and the response is the POST-redirect-to-owner-record with a flash slot that booking and owner edit already use. Cancellation belongs on the aggregate root, not on a repository. There is no VisitRepository and this slice must not add one (ADR 2026-07-31-feature-package-organization; system-design.md Contracts invariants): a visit reachable by its own identifier would let an identifier from one owner's record act on another's, whereas resolving owner then pet then visit makes edge cases 5 and 6 structural rather than checked. The three rules the cancellation enforces (the pet belongs to this owner, the visit belongs to that pet, the visit is upcoming) sit on Owner, Pet and Visit, not in the controller: architecture-principles.md Design Validation Checklist forbids a new business rule in a web controller, and the recorded controller-rule deviation explicitly does not extend to new rules. Suggested shape, source authoritative once written: Visit.isUpcoming() as a derived predicate stating the boundary booking already enforces (date != null and date.isAfter(LocalDate.now())), Pet.cancelVisit(Integer visitId) returning whether it happened, Owner.cancelVisit(Integer petId, Integer visitId) delegating through getPet(petId). Name it cancelVisit, not removeVisit or deleteVisit: ubiquitous-language.md Cancellation rejects Deletion and Removal as names for the clinic's act. BaseEntity.isNew() is the precedent for a derived predicate on a mapped entity; mapping is field-access here, so an unannotated getter is not persisted.
integration_points: Web surface: POST /owners/{ownerId}/pets/{petId}/visits/{visitId}/cancel in a new VisitCancellationController in the owner package. The handler loads the owner (unknown owner keeps the existing IllegalArgumentException convention of OwnerController.findOwner and VisitController.loadPetWithVisit), calls owner.cancelVisit(petId, visitId), saves through OwnerRepository and sets the message flash only when it returns true, sets the error flash and does not save when it returns false, and redirects to /owners/{ownerId} either way. The controller maps an outcome to a response; it branches on no domain state.

Why a new controller and not VisitController: VisitController's @ModelAttribute("visit") loadPetWithVisit runs before every handler in that class and calls pet.addVisit(new Visit()). A cancel handler added there would attach a blank visit to the loaded aggregate, and the subsequent owners.save(owner) would cascade-persist it, breaking acceptance criterion 'cancelling one visit leaves the pet, the owner, and that pet's other visits untouched'. This is a blocker on reuse, not a preference. The new class needs no @InitBinder: it binds path variables only, with no command object, so there is no id to disallow.

Template: ownerDetails.html renders the cancel action inside the existing per-visit row loop, guarded by th:if on the visit's upcoming test so a past visit carries no action. It must be a form with method post, never an anchor. The confirmation and refusal reuse the message and error alert slots already at the top of that page.
Persistence: Pet.visits gains orphanRemoval on its @OneToMany so a cancelled visit's row is deleted. Nothing else in the codebase removes from that collection today.

patterns.description: Owner.addVisit(petId, visit) is the shape to mirror: enter the aggregate at the root, resolve the pet by identity, delegate to it. Differs in one respect - addVisit asserts on an invalid pet identifier, while cancellation must return a refusal rather than throw, because a foreign or unknown visit is a refusal in the acceptance criteria, not a server error.

processNewVisitForm is the response pattern: POST, mutate through the owner, owners.save(owner), addFlashAttribute, redirect:/owners/{ownerId}. Its date guard at line 100 is the exact boundary Visit.isUpcoming() restates - a visit dated today is past.
The message and error alert slots the cancellation confirms and refuses into; both already exist and need no template plumbing.
@DataJpaTest against a real database with per-test rollback - the only place the orphan-removal delete can actually be observed. A MockMvc test with a mocked OwnerRepository cannot see it.

risks.risk: Removing a visit from Pet.visits without orphanRemoval issues UPDATE visits SET pet_id = NULL rather than a DELETE, because the association is unidirectional over a join column. visits.pet_id is nullable in all three vendor schemas, so the write succeeds silently and the row survives as an orphan. The page looks correct and every MockMvc test passes, while NG-10's 'no trace of a cancelled visit' is violated in the database.
risks.mitigation: Set orphanRemoval on the Pet.visits association, and prove the deletion in ClinicServiceTests rather than only at the controller level: flush, re-read the pet, and assert the visit is gone. Recorded in system-design.md Persistence and in the ADR.

risks.risk: spring.jpa.open-in-view is disabled, so the owner returned by findById is detached and owners.save is a merge. Orphan removal on a merged detached collection is correct Hibernate behaviour but is easy to get subtly wrong by mutating a different instance than the one saved.
risks.mitigation: Mutate and save the same Owner instance the handler loaded; the ClinicServiceTests-level assertion above is what catches a regression here.

risks.risk: A cancel action rendered as a link would make a state change reachable by GET - prefetchable, cacheable, and triggerable cross-origin by an img tag. The application has no CSRF protection anywhere (system-design.md Security Context), so a GET is the one shape that turns the absent control into an exploitable one.
risks.mitigation: Render a POST form. This matches every other mutation in the application; no new control is introduced, and none is weakened.

risks.risk: Distinguishing the three refusals in the response would leak whether a visit exists under another owner.
risks.mitigation: One boolean outcome, one refusal message for all three cases - a foreign pet, an unknown or already-cancelled visit, and a past visit are indistinguishable to the reader.

risks.risk: REQ-LANG-002: the existing flash messages in OwnerController and VisitController are hard-coded English, and I18nPropertiesSyncTest only scans templates, so copying that pattern would pass the build while breaching the requirement. Newly recorded as a defect row in system-design.md Known Defects.
risks.mitigation: Resolve the confirmation and refusal wording from the bundle through an injected MessageSource with LocaleContextHolder.getLocale(). Do not fix the existing three - that is a separate slice.

risks.risk: Visit.isUpcoming() reads LocalDate.now(), which is ambient state under architecture-principles.md Design Principle 3.
risks.mitigation: Accepted for this slice, matching the clock the booking guard already reads; tests fix a visit's status by choosing a date relative to today, as the existing suite does. Recorded as a consequence in the ADR. Introducing a Clock seam is a separate change touching booking too.

notes: Verdict is new rather than minor because two decisions here are hard to reverse and invisible from the existing code: the mapping-level orphan removal (whose failure mode is a silent null-FK write) and the placement of the first removal flow on the aggregate root rather than behind a new repository. Durable-memory writes made with this triage: docs/adr/2026-08-05-visit-cancellation-through-the-owner-aggregate.md (new), docs/adr/README.md index (added rows for that ADR and for the non-goal ADR the requirements author could not index), docs/system-design.md at Contracts (invariants paragraph, VisitCancellationController row, Implements updated on Owner, Pet and Visit), Persistence (orphan-removal rule), and Known Defects (English-only flash banners). Two corrections to the prd-entry, neither touching its acceptance criteria: (1) file_targets name VisitController.java and VisitControllerTests.java, but the design places the handler in a new VisitCancellationController for the blank-visit reason under integration_points - use the new class and its own test class instead; (2) the dispatch note says all eleven bundles need the new keys, but messages_en.properties is empty by design (English falls back to the base bundle, and I18nPropertiesSyncTest explicitly skips it) - add the keys to messages.properties and the nine translated bundles, leaving messages_en.properties empty. Three keys are needed: the cancel label, the confirmation, and the refusal. No design-doc-autofix records exist in the log, so the autofix audit is a no-op for this dispatch.

author: security-reviewer

findings.description: The threat model's attack-vector cell still reads "the owner, pet, or visit creation and edit routes". This slice adds the codebase's first destructive route, POST /owners/{ownerId}/pets/{petId}/visits/{visitId}/cancel, which any unauthenticated caller can drive and which hard-deletes the row (orphanRemoval = true) with no log, no reason, and no undo (NG-10). The row's mitigation cell is unchanged and still accurate, but the vector understates the delivered attack surface on exactly the change that makes the unmitigated threat materially worse: before this slice the worst an unauthenticated caller achieved was creating or altering a record that stays visible; now it can permanently erase one, and the erasure is by design untraceable. The Threat Model is the security artifact reviewers and operators read to size the demonstration's exposure, so it going stale here is the finding. Class sweep for stale mutation-surface claims across the security docs: the generic statements at docs/system-design.md:172 ("every mutating POST") and docs/security-principles.md:26 ("every route including every mutating one") already cover the new route and need no change; line 180 is the only instance.
findings.fix: Widen the vector cell to name deletion, e.g. "Any HTTP client POSTs to the owner, pet, or visit creation and edit routes, or to the visit cancellation route, which deletes the visit outright". Leave the mitigation cell as it stands.

approved_aspects: No VisitRepository and no by-bare-id visit lookup: a repository-wide grep for VisitRepository returns nothing, and the only cancellation path resolves owner -> pet -> visit through OwnerRepository.findById(ownerId), Owner.getPet(petId), then Pet.cancelVisit(visitId) over the pet's own in-memory collection. A visitId belonging to another owner's pet simply does not match any element, so the foreign-owner refusal is structural rather than a check that could be forgotten. Owner.cancelVisit and Pet.cancelVisit both null-guard their identifiers before touching the collection.

POST-only shape holds: the handler is @PostMapping with no @RequestMapping or GET fallback, and the template renders a method=post form rather than a link, so the destructive action is not reachable by GET and will not fire from a prefetch, a crawler, or a pasted URL. What it does not buy, given no CSRF token anywhere in the app, is protection from a cross-site form POST. That is not in scope for this slice: the app has no authentication and no session, so a cross-site POST confers nothing a direct POST does not already confer -- there is no ambient authority to ride. The condition is app-wide and pre-existing, recorded in docs/system-design.md Security Context and docs/security-principles.md:26, which instruct reviewers not to raise it as a defect. Adding a token here alone would not change the exposure.

Uniform refusal is genuinely uniform: all three refusal cases converge on one boolean false from Owner.cancelVisit, one message key (visitCancellationRefused), and one redirect to /owners/{ownerId} with the same 302 shape. Response shape carries no oracle. Timing carries none either -- the pet and visit collections are EAGER-fetched by the single findById, so all three refusals walk the same already-loaded in-memory collections and issue no further query; no refusal path performs work proportional to what exists under another owner. The success path does differ in timing (it issues save + DELETE), but success/refusal is information the caller already holds.

author: product-requirements-expert
title: Staff can cancel an upcoming visit from the owner's record
summary: The owner's record offers a cancel action beside each upcoming visit of each pet. Cancelling takes that visit off the pet's record and confirms on the owner's record. A visit dated today or earlier is history: it carries no cancel action, and a direct cancellation request for it is refused.
acceptance_criteria: given a pet with an upcoming visit, when the owner's record is opened, then a cancel action is offered beside that visit
given a pet with a visit dated today or earlier, when the owner's record is opened, then no cancel action is offered beside that visit
given an upcoming visit, when it is cancelled, then the owner's record is shown again, the cancellation is confirmed there, and the visit no longer appears under its pet
given a cancelled visit, when a new visit is booked for the same pet, then the cancelled visit is not among the earlier visits shown
given a visit dated today or earlier, when its cancellation is requested directly, then the request is refused and the visit remains on the record
edge case 3: the date boundary is the one booking enforces — a visit dated today is past, not upcoming
edge case 4: cancelling one visit leaves the pet, the owner, and that pet's other visits untouched
edge case 5: a request to cancel a visit belonging to a different owner's pet than the one named is refused
edge case 6: a repeated request to cancel a visit already cancelled is refused rather than confirmed a second time
non_goals: amending a visit — changing its date, its description, or the pet it stands against (NG-5)
any trace of a cancelled visit: no cancellation log, no reason, no undo, no view of what was cancelled (NG-10)
cancelling a visit from the booking page; the action lives on the owner's record only
deleting an owner or a pet (NG-4)
cancelling or otherwise altering a visit dated today or earlier
